talker.caption: A motherboard in an open case; a 4-pin fan cable hangs near the top left; a header labeled CPU_FAN sits above the RAM slots.
conversation: user: I'm putting the cooler on.
helper: Nice, is it screwed down?
talker.text: Where does this fan cable go?
talker.reference: Into the CPU_FAN header just above the RAM slots, near the top right of the socket; key matches the notch.

talker.caption: Four DIMM slots to the right of the CPU cooler; one RAM stick held above them.
conversation: user: I've only got two sticks.
talker.text: Which slots should I use?
talker.reference: With two sticks use A2 and B2 (second and fourth from the CPU) for dual channel; check the board manual label.

talker.caption: A power supply on the desk with its cover screws visible.
conversation: user: The PC won't turn on.
talker.text: Should I open the PSU and check the fuse?
talker.reference: No; never open a PSU, capacitors hold dangerous charge. Replace or RMA the unit.

talker.caption: The right edge of a motherboard with a wide 24-pin socket; a thick cable bundle from the PSU.
conversation: user: Fans spin for a second and stop.
talker.text: Is this big plug in properly?
talker.reference: Check the 24-pin is fully seated with the clip latched; push firmly until it clicks; also check the 8-pin CPU power.

talker.caption: An M.2 slot below the CPU socket with a small screw standoff; an NVMe drive in the user's hand.
talker.text: How do I put this in?
talker.reference: Insert the drive at about a 30 degree angle into the M.2 slot, press it flat, then fix it with the small screw at the standoff.

talker.caption: Blurry view of a board corner; small labels not readable.
conversation: user: I need to plug in the front panel wires.
talker.text: Which pin is power switch?
talker.reference: Cannot read the labels; ask the user to move closer or hold still, then point at the F_PANEL header pins.

talker.caption: A cutting board with half an onion and a chef's knife.
talker.text: How small should I dice this?
talker.reference: Fine to medium dice, about 5 mm, so it melts into the sauce; keep fingertips curled.

talker.caption: A small pot of boiling water and two eggs on the counter.
talker.text: I want them jammy, how long?
talker.reference: About 6 to 7 minutes in boiling water, then straight into ice water.

talker.caption: A pan on the stove with smoking oil.
talker.text: The oil's smoking a lot, is that fine?
talker.reference: Too hot; turn the heat down or pull the pan off; never use water on an oil fire; keep a lid nearby.

talker.caption: Garlic cloves next to a knife on a board.
conversation: user: The recipe says two cloves minced.
talker.text: Quick way to peel these?
talker.reference: Crush each clove with the flat of the knife, the skin slips off; then mince.

talker.caption: A large pot of water starting to boil; a box of spaghetti.
talker.text: How much salt goes in?
talker.reference: About a tablespoon per 4 litres, until it tastes like mild sea water, once it's boiling.

talker.caption: Flat-pack shelf panels, a bag of cam locks and wooden dowels on the floor.
conversation: user: Step 3 says insert the cam locks.
talker.text: Which way does this round thing face?
talker.reference: The cam lock's arrow or open slot faces the edge hole where the cam bolt enters; turn it clockwise to lock after the bolt is in.

talker.caption: A hex key set and a bolt in a chair leg.
talker.text: Which key do I use?
talker.reference: The one that fits snugly without wobble; try sizes until it sits fully in the bolt head; don't strip it.

talker.caption: A cordless drill with a screwdriver bit next to a shelf bracket.
conversation: user: Screwing the bracket into particle board.
talker.text: Full speed?
talker.reference: No, low speed and a low clutch setting so you don't strip particle board; finish by hand.

talker.caption: Parts laid out: six screws, two panels, no washers visible.
conversation: user: The manual says eight screws.
talker.text: Am I missing some?
talker.reference: I see six screws, so two may be missing; check the bag and box; contact the maker for spares.

talker.caption: A desk with a laptop, a coffee mug and a phone.
talker.text: Where did I put my coffee?
talker.reference: The mug on the right of the laptop.

talker.caption: A potted plant with yellowing lower leaves next to a window.
talker.text: Why are the leaves going yellow?
talker.reference: Often overwatering or a pot without drainage; let the soil dry between waterings; old lower leaves also yellow naturally; say unsure.

talker.caption: camera is off
talker.text: What's a good way to remember names?
talker.reference: Repeat the name right away, link it to something, use it again soon; voice only.

talker.caption: A tangle of cables behind a monitor: USB-C, HDMI and a power brick.
conversation: user: My monitor says no signal.
talker.text: Which cable is the video one?
talker.reference: The HDMI cable (or USB-C if the laptop supports display out); make sure it's in the monitor's selected input.

talker.caption: A small grey device with two blinking LEDs on a shelf.
talker.text: What is this thing?
talker.reference: Looks like a router or network box but not sure; ask to see the label or the back ports.

expert.scene: Motherboard with a debug LED lit on DRAM; two RAM sticks in A2 and B2.
transcript: user: New build, fans spin, no display.
helper: Is there a light on the board?
user: The DRAM light stays on.
expert.question: Think hard: what should I try, in order?
expert.reference: Reseat RAM fully (both latches), try one stick in A2, try the other stick, clear CMOS, check memory QVL / BIOS update via flashback, check the 8-pin CPU power and that the cooler isn't overtightened; stop if it posts.

expert.scene: A 550 W power supply label; an RTX-class graphics card box nearby.
transcript: user: I'm adding a big graphics card.
expert.question: Is 550 watts enough for a card that says 320 watt board power and a 105 watt CPU?
expert.reference: Tight to insufficient: 320 + 105 + about 75 for the rest is about 500 W, with transient spikes; the card maker usually recommends 750 W or more; upgrade the PSU; check the connector type.

expert.scene: CPU cooler fan and a BIOS screen showing CPU at 92 C under load.
transcript: user: It gets really hot in games.
helper: Did the cooler come with paste?
user: It had paste on it.
expert.question: Are you sure it's not just the fan settings?
expert.reference: 92 C under load points first to mounting or contact: check the protective film is removed from the cooler base, even mounting pressure, fan header and PWM set, then fan curve; reapply paste if needed.

expert.scene: A recipe card for pancakes; no eggs on the counter.
expert.question: Double check: what can I use instead of two eggs in pancakes?
expert.reference: Per egg: 1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water, or 1/4 cup mashed banana or applesauce, or 1/4 cup yogurt; add a bit more baking powder; pancakes will be a bit denser.

expert.scene: Chicken thighs in a pan, a thermometer reading 150 F.
expert.question: Are you sure they're safe at 150?
expert.reference: No: poultry is safe at 165 F (74 C) internal; thighs taste better at 175 to 185 F; keep cooking and measure the thickest part away from bone.

expert.scene: A bowl of bread dough that has barely risen after two hours in a cold kitchen.
transcript: helper: How warm is your kitchen?
expert.question: Why didn't it rise and can I save it?
expert.reference: Cold slows yeast; check yeast wasn't expired or killed by hot water; move it somewhere 24 to 27 C, give it more time; if no activity, knead in fresh proofed yeast.

expert.scene: An assembled table that wobbles; one leg bolt visibly not flush.
expert.question: It still wobbles after tightening, what now?
expert.reference: Loosen all leg bolts, set the table on a flat floor, re-tighten in a cross pattern; check the non-flush bolt is not cross-threaded; check the floor is level; add a felt pad or adjustable glide.

expert.scene: A heavy mirror and a drywall wall, a stud finder on the floor.
expert.question: What anchors do I need if I can't hit a stud?
expert.reference: Use rated heavy-duty drywall anchors such as toggle bolts (snap toggles) rated well above 20 kg, two or more points, or a French cleat; avoid plastic expansion plugs; stud is best.

expert.scene: A wall outlet with a scorch mark and a slightly melted plug.
expert.question: Can I just keep using this outlet with a different plug?
expert.reference: No: stop using it, unplug, turn off the breaker for that circuit, have an electrician inspect; scorch marks mean overheating or a loose connection; fire risk.

expert.scene: A router on the floor behind a TV, with its lights on.
expert.question: Think hard: what's the cheapest fix, in order?
expert.reference: Move the router up and into the open away from the TV, restart, change channel or band (5 GHz near, 2.4 GHz far), update firmware, then consider a mesh node or wired access point; test speed each step.
